result_healthy.en: These leaves look healthy. No sign of rust, leaf miner or leaf spot was seen. This check covers leaves only, not berries.
result_healthy.sw: Majani haya yanaonekana kuwa na afya. Hakuna dalili ya kutu, wadudu wanaochimba ndani ya majani, wala madoa ya ugonjwa. Ukaguzi huu ni wa majani tu, si wa matunda.
result_healthy.kik: Mathangũ maya ma kahũa nĩ mega. Hakuna dalili ya kutu, wadudu wanaochimba ndani ya majani, wala madoa ya ugonjwa. Ukaguzi huu ni wa majani tu, si wa matunda.
result_healthy.sw_backtranslation_en: These leaves appear to be healthy. There are no signs of corrosion, pests digging in the leaves, or patches of disease. This examination is for the leaves only, not the fruits.
result_healthy.kik_phrase: Mathangũ maya ma kahũa nĩ mega.
result_healthy.kik_backtranslation_en: These coffee leaves are good. There are no signs of fever, no worms in the grass, no spots of disease. It's only the grass, not the fruit.
result_healthy.notes: Not a disease result, so no final-call line; states the leaf-only limit instead. kik is a short phrase meaning 'These coffee leaves are good' (not 'healthy'); the rest falls back to Swahili. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): re-check of the revised line (Oct 3): meaning kept ('pests digging in the leaves'); 'kutu' still came back as 'corrosion', the same Swahili word as metal rust. The kik field = a short Kikuyu phrase ('Mathangũ maya ma kahũa nĩ mega.') that replaces the first Swahili sentence, followed by the remaining Swahili sentences, so nothing is dropped. Kikuyu back-translation (NLLB kik->eng, FLORES chrF++ 42.9, weak evidence): 'These coffee leaves are good. There are no signs of fever, no worms in the grass, no spots of disease. It's only the grass, not the fruit.'. Revised Oct 3 after the machine cross-check; see docs/SWAHILI_CHECK.md.

result_rust.en: This looks like coffee leaf rust. Rust shows as yellow-orange powder under the leaf. The extension officer makes the final call.
result_rust.sw: Hii inaonekana kama ugonjwa wa kutu ya majani ya kahawa. Kutu huonekana kama unga wa manjano au rangi ya chungwa chini ya jani. Afisa wa ugani ndiye atakayefanya uamuzi wa mwisho.
result_rust.sw_backtranslation_en: This looks like a disease of coffee leaf rust. The rash appears as a yellowish-colored powder or a peachy color underneath the leaf. The extension officer will make the final decision.
result_rust.notes: Symptoms per KCS 8.4.2 (pale yellow spots on the underside turning to yellow/orange powdery masses). 'kutu' = rust. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): Meaning kept; 'kutu' rendered as 'rash' in sentence two (word-sense slip). Sources: KCS = Kenya Coffee Sustainability Manual (review led by KALRO Coffee Research Institute with AFA Coffee Directorate and partners), https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/KCS-MANUAL-review-03112020.pdf

result_miner.en: This looks like leaf miner damage. It shows as dry brown patches on the leaf. The extension officer makes the final call.
result_miner.sw: Hii inaonekana kama uharibifu wa wadudu wanaochimba ndani ya majani. Huonekana kama sehemu kubwa kavu za rangi ya kahawia kwenye jani. Afisa wa ugani ndiye atakayefanya uamuzi wa mwisho.
result_miner.sw_backtranslation_en: This looks like the destruction of insects that dig into the leaves. It looks like a large dry brownish patch on the leaf. The extension officer will make the final decision.
result_miner.notes: Symptoms per KCS 9.5.8 and INFONET (irregular brown blotches on the upper side of leaves). Simplification: the protocol photographs the underside; mines are clearest from above. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): re-check of the revised line (Oct 3): meaning kept ('insects that dig into the leaves', 'a large dry brownish patch on the leaf'). Sources: KCS = Kenya Coffee Sustainability Manual (review led by KALRO Coffee Research Institute with AFA Coffee Directorate and partners), https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/KCS-MANUAL-review-03112020.pdf | INFONET = Infonet-Biovision (Kenya), Coffee (Revised), https://infonet-biovision.org/crops-fruits-vegetables/coffee-revised Revised Oct 3 after the machine cross-check; see docs/SWAHILI_CHECK.md.

result_cercospora.en: This looks like brown eye spot. It shows as round brown spots with a pale centre. The extension officer makes the final call.
result_cercospora.sw: Hii inaonekana kama ugonjwa wa madoa ya kahawia. Huonekana kama madoa ya mviringo ya kahawia, yenye rangi nyeupe katikati. Afisa wa ugani ndiye atakayefanya uamuzi wa mwisho.
result_cercospora.sw_backtranslation_en: This looks like brown spots. They look like round brown spots, with a white color in the center. The extension officer will make the final decision.
result_cercospora.notes: Brown eye spot = Cercospora coffeicola (PLANTWISE_BES, LUCID_BES). KCS lists it as a minor disease in Kenya. Swahili name is descriptive ('brown spot disease'), not a confirmed standard term. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): Meaning kept. The Swahili disease name is descriptive ('brown spot disease'). Sources: KCS = Kenya Coffee Sustainability Manual (review led by KALRO Coffee Research Institute with AFA Coffee Directorate and partners), https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/KCS-MANUAL-review-03112020.pdf | PLANTWISE_BES = CABI PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank, Cercospora coffeicola (brown eye spot), https://plantwiseplusknowledgebank.org/doi/full/10.1079/pwkb.20207800275 | LUCID_BES = Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds fact sheet: Coffee brown-eye spot, https://apps.lucidcentral.org/ppp/text/web_full/entities/coffee_browneye_spot_142.htm

result_phoma.en: This looks like Phoma leaf spot. It shows as dark patches, often on young leaves after cold weather. The extension officer makes the final call.
result_phoma.sw: Hii inaonekana kama ugonjwa wa Phoma. Huonekana kama madoa meusi, mara nyingi kwenye majani machanga baada ya baridi. Afisa wa ugani ndiye atakayefanya uamuzi wa mwisho.
result_phoma.sw_backtranslation_en: This looks like Phoma's disease. It appears as black spots, often on young leaves after the cold. The extension officer will make the final decision.
result_phoma.notes: Phoma (Ascochyta) tarda; favoured by cold wind at high altitude (PHOMA sources are mostly Brazilian). KCS lists 'leaf blight and stem die back' as minor in Kenya. 'Phoma' is spelled as in English; TTS may not pronounce it well. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): Meaning kept. Sources: KCS = Kenya Coffee Sustainability Manual (review led by KALRO Coffee Research Institute with AFA Coffee Directorate and partners), https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/KCS-MANUAL-review-03112020.pdf | PHOMA = Phoma (Ascochyta) tarda leaf spot: Cultivar Magazine, https://revistacultivar.com/articles/phoma-spot-or-ascochyta-spot-of-coffee ; Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascochyta_tarda

result_not_sure.en: Not sure. The tool cannot tell from this photo. The photo is saved for the officer to look at.
result_not_sure.sw: Sina uhakika. Siwezi kutambua kutoka kwenye picha hii. Picha imehifadhiwa ili afisa wa ugani aiangalie.
result_not_sure.kik: Ndiĩ. Siwezi kutambua kutoka kwenye picha hii. Picha imehifadhiwa ili afisa wa ugani aiangalie.
result_not_sure.sw_backtranslation_en: I'm not sure. I can't tell from this picture. The picture has been saved for a fiction agent to look at.
result_not_sure.kik_backtranslation_en: I do not know. I can't figure out where this picture came from. The images are hidden so that the fake agent can look at them.
result_not_sure.notes: kik phrase means 'I do not know'; the rest of the Swahili text follows it. The abstain lane (fail-safe required by the brief). Shown when confidence is low or the photo looks unlike the training data. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): 'afisa wa ugani' came back as 'fiction agent' here only; the same phrase back-translates as 'extension officer' in other strings. The kik field = a short Kikuyu phrase ('Ndiĩ.') that replaces the first Swahili sentence, followed by the remaining Swahili sentences, so nothing is dropped. Kikuyu back-translation (NLLB kik->eng, FLORES chrF++ 42.9, weak evidence): 'I do not know. I can't figure out where this picture came from. The images are hidden so that the fake agent can look at them.'. Machine transcription did not recognise the 0.5 s Kikuyu clip (heard 'ĩe'); a recorded human clip would be clearer.

retake_photo.en: Please take the photo again. Show the underside of one leaf, in daylight. Hold the phone still.
retake_photo.sw: Tafadhali piga picha tena. Onyesha upande wa chini wa jani moja, kwenye mwanga wa mchana. Shika simu bila kutikisa.
retake_photo.kik: Oya mbica ĩngĩ. Onyesha upande wa chini wa jani moja, kwenye mwanga wa mchana. Shika simu bila kutikisa.
retake_photo.sw_backtranslation_en: Please take another picture. Point to the bottom of one leaf, in daylight. Hold the phone without shaking.
retake_photo.kik_backtranslation_en: Take another picture. Look at the bottom of one leaf, and see the light of day. Keep your phone on.
retake_photo.notes: Photo protocol of the app: underside of 3 leaves on each of 5 trees. kik phrase means 'Take another photo'; the rest falls back to Swahili. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): 'upande wa chini' came back as 'bottom' (= underside). The kik field = a short Kikuyu phrase ('Oya mbica ĩngĩ.') that replaces the first Swahili sentence, followed by the remaining Swahili sentences, so nothing is dropped. Kikuyu back-translation (NLLB kik->eng, FLORES chrF++ 42.9, weak evidence): 'Take another picture. Look at the bottom of one leaf, and see the light of day. Keep your phone on.'.

action_healthy.en: Keep up good care. Prune on time, weed, and feed the trees as advised. Check again at the next visit.
action_healthy.sw: Endelea kutunza vizuri. Pogoa kwa wakati, ondoa magugu, na weka mbolea kama ulivyoshauriwa. Kagua tena katika ziara ijayo.
action_healthy.sw_backtranslation_en: Keep taking good care of them. Cut it in time, remove the weeds, and place the fertilizer as instructed. Review it again on your next visit.
action_healthy.notes: General good practice per KCS modules 4, 6, 7. 'Feed as advised' avoids giving fertiliser types or rates. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): 'Pogoa' came back as 'cut' (= prune). Sources: KCS = Kenya Coffee Sustainability Manual (review led by KALRO Coffee Research Institute with AFA Coffee Directorate and partners), https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/KCS-MANUAL-review-03112020.pdf

action_rust.en: Mark this tree. Prune so air and light reach the leaves. Ask the extension officer about approved rust control before the rains.
action_rust.sw: Weka alama kwenye mti huu. Pogoa matawi ili hewa na mwanga vifikie majani. Muulize afisa wa ugani kuhusu njia zilizoidhinishwa za kudhibiti kutu kabla ya mvua.
action_rust.sw_backtranslation_en: Make a mark on this tree. Cut off the branches so that the air and light reach the leaves. Ask an expansion officer about approved methods for controlling corrosion before rain.
action_rust.notes: KCS 8.4.2: cultural control by proper and timely pruning; control must start before the rains and follow the CRI programme with PCPB-registered products. CLR_REVIEW: pruning and shading are key cultural practices. No product, ingredient or dose is named on purpose. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): Meaning kept; 'kutu' rendered as 'corrosion'. Sources: KCS = Kenya Coffee Sustainability Manual (review led by KALRO Coffee Research Institute with AFA Coffee Directorate and partners), https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/KCS-MANUAL-review-03112020.pdf | CLR_REVIEW = Coffee Leaf Rust (Hemileia vastatrix) in Kenya - A Review, Agronomy 2021, 11(12):2590, https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4395/11/12/2590

action_miner.en: Mark this tree. Small wasps kill many leaf miners, so do not spray without advice. Ask the extension officer what to do.
action_miner.sw: Weka alama kwenye mti huu. Nyigu wadogo huua wadudu wengi wa aina hii, kwa hiyo usinyunyize dawa bila ushauri. Muulize afisa wa ugani hatua za kuchukua.
action_miner.sw_backtranslation_en: Make a mark on this tree. Small ants kill many of these insects, so don't spray them without advice. Ask the extension officer what steps to take.
action_miner.notes: INFONET: parasitic wasps and predatory mites give natural control of leaf miners. KCS 9.5.8: control products are specific registered types, so the choice is left to the officer. Simplification: 'kill' covers parasitism. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): 'Nyigu' (wasp) came back as 'ants'. Dictionaries give 'wasp' (docs/SWAHILI_CHECK.md section 6); the speaker review in pilot week 1 checks it. Sources: KCS = Kenya Coffee Sustainability Manual (review led by KALRO Coffee Research Institute with AFA Coffee Directorate and partners), https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/KCS-MANUAL-review-03112020.pdf | INFONET = Infonet-Biovision (Kenya), Coffee (Revised), https://infonet-biovision.org/crops-fruits-vegetables/coffee-revised

action_cercospora.en: Brown eye spot is common on weak, underfed trees. Ask the officer about a soil test and feeding. Mulch to keep soil moist.
action_cercospora.sw: Ugonjwa wa madoa ya kahawia hutokea sana kwenye miti dhaifu isiyo na mbolea ya kutosha. Muulize afisa wa ugani kuhusu kupima udongo, na kuhusu mbolea inayofaa. Weka matandazo ili udongo ubaki na unyevu.
action_cercospora.sw_backtranslation_en: Brown spot disease occurs most commonly on weak trees with insufficient fertilizer. Ask the land surveyor about soil measurement, and about suitable fertilizer. Place nets so that the soil remains moist.
action_cercospora.notes: PLANTWISE_BES: nitrogen and potassium shortage and plant stress raise susceptibility; do a soil analysis. KCS 4.6: soil samples go to CRI; KCS 3.7.1: mulch conserves moisture. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): re-check of the revised line (Oct 3): the soil test and the fertiliser advice now come back as two separate points. Two key words still come back wrong: 'afisa wa ugani' as 'land surveyor' and 'matandazo' (mulch) as 'nets'. Published Kenyan and Tanzanian sources use both words (docs/SWAHILI_CHECK.md section 6), so we kept them; a speaker should confirm. Sources: KCS = Kenya Coffee Sustainability Manual (review led by KALRO Coffee Research Institute with AFA Coffee Directorate and partners), https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/KCS-MANUAL-review-03112020.pdf | PLANTWISE_BES = CABI PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank, Cercospora coffeicola (brown eye spot), https://plantwiseplusknowledgebank.org/doi/full/10.1079/pwkb.20207800275 Revised Oct 3 after the machine cross-check; see docs/SWAHILI_CHECK.md.

action_phoma.en: Phoma is worse in cold, windy weather on high ground. Windbreak and shade trees can help. Ask the extension officer about approved control.
action_phoma.sw: Ugonjwa wa Phoma huzidi wakati wa baridi na upepo mkali katika maeneo ya juu. Miti ya kuzuia upepo na miti ya kivuli inaweza kusaidia. Muulize afisa wa ugani kuhusu njia zilizoidhinishwa za kudhibiti ugonjwa huu.
action_phoma.sw_backtranslation_en: Phoma's disease is more common in the cold and high winds. Windmills and shade trees can help. Ask a medical examiner about approved treatments for the disease.
action_phoma.notes: PHOMA sources: cold wind and altitude above about 900 m favour the disease. Windbreak advice is general (Infonet-Biovision recommends windbreaks on exposed sides for bacterial blight, and the PHOMA article for Phoma; KCS does not mention them). Kenyan sources are thinnest for this item; a KALRO Coffee Research Institute agronomist should confirm. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): re-check of the revised line (Oct 3): 'Ugonjwa wa Phoma' now comes back as a disease ('Phoma's disease'). Two key words still come back wrong: 'miti ya kuzuia upepo' (windbreak trees) as 'windmills' and 'afisa wa ugani' as 'medical examiner'. Sources confirm both terms (docs/SWAHILI_CHECK.md section 6); a speaker should confirm. Sources: KCS = Kenya Coffee Sustainability Manual (review led by KALRO Coffee Research Institute with AFA Coffee Directorate and partners), https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/KCS-MANUAL-review-03112020.pdf | PHOMA = Phoma (Ascochyta) tarda leaf spot: Cultivar Magazine, https://revistacultivar.com/articles/phoma-spot-or-ascochyta-spot-of-coffee ; Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascochyta_tarda Revised Oct 3 after the machine cross-check; see docs/SWAHILI_CHECK.md.

action_not_sure.en: Put a mark on this tree. The officer will review the saved photo. Do not spray because of this result. Wait for the officer's advice first.
action_not_sure.sw: Weka alama kwenye mti huu. Afisa wa ugani ataangalia picha iliyohifadhiwa. Usinyunyize dawa kwa sababu ya matokeo haya. Subiri ushauri wa afisa kwanza.
action_not_sure.sw_backtranslation_en: Make a mark on this tree. An extension officer will look at the saved image. Do not spray medication because of these effects. Wait for the officer's advice first.
action_not_sure.notes: Abstain lane: no action is taken on an uncertain result; the photo waits in the officer queue. The Swahili says 'put a mark' (not 'ribbon'), as the other two action lines do, and adds 'Wait for the officer's advice first'. The English was updated on Oct 3 to match (mark the tree; wait for the officer's advice). Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): re-check of the revised line (Oct 3): meaning kept ('Make a mark on this tree', 'Do not spray', 'Wait for the officer's advice first'); 'matokeo' (results) came back as 'effects'. Revised Oct 3 after the machine cross-check; see docs/SWAHILI_CHECK.md.

plot_all_healthy.en: All photos from this plot look healthy. Keep checking at each visit. Leaf photos cannot show berry problems.
plot_all_healthy.sw: Majani katika picha zote za shamba hili yanaonekana kuwa na afya. Endelea kukagua katika kila ziara. Picha za majani haziwezi kuonyesha matatizo ya matunda.
plot_all_healthy.sw_backtranslation_en: The leaves in all the pictures of this garden seem healthy. Keep reviewing each visit. Pictures of the leaves cannot reveal the problems of the fruit.
plot_all_healthy.notes: Reminds that coffee berry disease and berry borer are not visible on leaves (see checklist). A Kikuyu phrase ('Mĩtĩ yothe nĩ mĩega', all the trees are good) was dropped: it claims more than the photos show. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): re-check of the revised line (Oct 3): meaning kept; the line now says the leaves look healthy, not the photos. Revised Oct 3 after the machine cross-check; see docs/SWAHILI_CHECK.md.

plot_some_problem.en: Some photos show a possible problem. Please show this card to the extension officer.
plot_some_problem.sw: Baadhi ya picha zinaonyesha kwamba huenda kuna tatizo. Tafadhali mwonyeshe afisa wa ugani kadi hii.
plot_some_problem.sw_backtranslation_en: Some pictures suggest that there may be a problem. Please show this card to the expansion officer.
plot_some_problem.notes: Plot card when 1-2 photos on one tree show a disease answer (app rule). The user decides when to share; the app sends nothing by itself. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): re-check of the revised line (Oct 3): meaning kept ('there may be a problem'); 'afisa wa ugani' came back as 'expansion officer'. Revised Oct 3 after the machine cross-check; see docs/SWAHILI_CHECK.md.

plot_officer_alert.en: There may be a problem on several trees in this plot. Please show this card to the extension officer soon. The officer decides what to do.
plot_officer_alert.sw: Huenda kuna tatizo kwenye miti kadhaa katika shamba hili. Tafadhali mwonyeshe afisa wa ugani kadi hii mapema. Afisa ndiye ataamua hatua za kuchukua.
plot_officer_alert.sw_backtranslation_en: There may be a problem with some of the trees in this garden. Please show the expansion officer this card in advance. It is up to the official to decide what steps to take.
plot_officer_alert.notes: Plot card when a disease answer appears on 2 or more trees or in 3 or more photos (app rule in app.js plotVerdict). It is a prompt to the user, not an automatic message to the officer. The disease may be any of the four, so rust is not named. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): Meaning kept; 'kadhaa' (several) came back as 'some', 'mapema' (soon) as 'in advance'.

check_q1_old_trees.en: Are most trees old, with few new branches? If yes, ask the officer about stumping to renew them.
check_q1_old_trees.sw: Je, miti mingi imezeeka, na ina matawi mapya machache? Kama ndiyo, muulize afisa wa ugani kuhusu kukata mashina ili miti ichipue upya.
check_q1_old_trees.sw_backtranslation_en: Are many trees old, with few new branches? If so, ask an expansion officer about cutting the stems so that the trees can bloom again.
check_q1_old_trees.notes: Non-AI checklist. KCS 3.8-3.9 and 6.6: rehabilitation by clean stumping or change of cycle renews aging, underproductive trees. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): re-check of the revised line (Oct 3): 'kukata mashina' came back as 'cutting the stems', no longer 'cutting down trees'; 'afisa wa ugani' came back as 'expansion officer'. Sources: KCS = Kenya Coffee Sustainability Manual (review led by KALRO Coffee Research Institute with AFA Coffee Directorate and partners), https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/KCS-MANUAL-review-03112020.pdf Revised Oct 3 after the machine cross-check; see docs/SWAHILI_CHECK.md.

check_q2_no_fertiliser.en: Has the coffee gone without manure or fertiliser this year? If yes, ask the co-op about a soil test first.
check_q2_no_fertiliser.sw: Je, kahawa imekosa mbolea ya samadi au mbolea ya dukani mwaka huu? Kama ndiyo, uliza chama cha ushirika kuhusu kupima udongo kwanza.
check_q2_no_fertiliser.sw_backtranslation_en: Has there been a shortage of coffee fertilizer or store fertilizer this year? If so, ask a cooperative about the soil survey first.
check_q2_no_fertiliser.notes: Non-AI checklist. KCS 4.6: soil analysis every 2-3 years, samples sent to CRI; KCS warns against fertiliser use without soil analysis. Worded so that YES means a possible cause, like the other questions. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): 'mbolea ya samadi' (manure) was lost; came back as 'coffee fertilizer or store fertilizer'. Sources: KCS = Kenya Coffee Sustainability Manual (review led by KALRO Coffee Research Institute with AFA Coffee Directorate and partners), https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/KCS-MANUAL-review-03112020.pdf

check_q3_weeding.en: Are there many weeds under the coffee? If yes, weed before feeding the trees. Weeds take water and food.
check_q3_weeding.sw: Je, kuna magugu mengi chini ya kahawa? Kama ndiyo, ondoa magugu kabla ya kuweka mbolea. Magugu huchukua maji na chakula cha mimea.
check_q3_weeding.sw_backtranslation_en: Is there a lot of weeds underneath the coffee? If so, remove the weeds before fertilizing them. Weeds absorb water and nutrients from plants.
check_q3_weeding.notes: Non-AI checklist. KCS 7.4: weed before fertiliser is applied, so weeds do not take it up. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): Meaning kept. Sources: KCS = Kenya Coffee Sustainability Manual (review led by KALRO Coffee Research Institute with AFA Coffee Directorate and partners), https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/KCS-MANUAL-review-03112020.pdf

check_q4_berry_spots.en: Do green berries have dark, sunken spots? This may be coffee berry disease. Show the extension officer soon.
check_q4_berry_spots.sw: Je, matunda mabichi yana madoa meusi yaliyozama ndani? Huenda ni ugonjwa wa matunda ya kahawa. Mwonyeshe afisa wa ugani mapema.
check_q4_berry_spots.sw_backtranslation_en: Do green fruits have deep black spots? It may be a disease of the coffee fruit. Show the expansion officer in advance.
check_q4_berry_spots.notes: Non-AI checklist; referral only. KCS 8.4.1: CBD shows as small dark sunken lesions on green berries and can cause total crop loss. The leaf model cannot see this. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): 'yaliyozama ndani' (sunken) came back as 'deep'. Sources: KCS = Kenya Coffee Sustainability Manual (review led by KALRO Coffee Research Institute with AFA Coffee Directorate and partners), https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/KCS-MANUAL-review-03112020.pdf

check_q5_berry_holes.en: Do berries have a small round hole near the tip? This may be berry borer. Collect fallen berries and tell the officer.
check_q5_berry_holes.sw: Je, matunda yana tundu dogo la mviringo karibu na ncha? Huenda ni mdudu anayetoboa matunda. Okota matunda yaliyoanguka na umwambie afisa wa ugani.
check_q5_berry_holes.sw_backtranslation_en: Does the fruit have a small round hole near the tip? It may be a fruit picking insect. Pick up the fallen fruit and tell the rumor officer.
check_q5_berry_holes.notes: Non-AI checklist. KCS 9.5.2 and INFONET: one or two small round holes near the tip of berries; collect infested fallen berries (field hygiene). The leaf model cannot see this. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): 'mdudu anayetoboa matunda' (berry-boring insect) came back as 'fruit picking insect'; 'afisa wa ugani' -> 'rumor officer'. Sources: KCS = Kenya Coffee Sustainability Manual (review led by KALRO Coffee Research Institute with AFA Coffee Directorate and partners), https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/KCS-MANUAL-review-03112020.pdf | INFONET = Infonet-Biovision (Kenya), Coffee (Revised), https://infonet-biovision.org/crops-fruits-vegetables/coffee-revised

check_q6_dry_flowering.en: Was there a long dry spell during flowering? That can mean fewer berries. Mulch helps keep the soil moist.
check_q6_dry_flowering.sw: Je, kulikuwa na kiangazi kirefu wakati wa kuchanua maua? Hilo linaweza kusababisha matunda machache. Matandazo husaidia udongo kubaki na unyevu.
check_q6_dry_flowering.sw_backtranslation_en: Was there a long summer when flowers bloomed? This may result in little fruitage. Grids help the soil to stay moist.
check_q6_dry_flowering.notes: Non-AI checklist. KCS 5.5: critical water periods include flower buds formed with no rain and early fruit (pinhead) stage; KCS 3.7.1: mulch conserves moisture. Simplification: weather is asked, not measured. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): 'kiangazi' (dry season) came back as 'summer'; 'matandazo' (mulch) as 'grids'. Sources: KCS = Kenya Coffee Sustainability Manual (review led by KALRO Coffee Research Institute with AFA Coffee Directorate and partners), https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/KCS-MANUAL-review-03112020.pdf

disclaimer_final_call.en: This tool can be wrong. It gives a first look only. The extension officer makes the final call.
disclaimer_final_call.sw: Programu hii inaweza kukosea. Inatoa jibu la awali tu. Afisa wa ugani ndiye atakayefanya uamuzi wa mwisho.
disclaimer_final_call.sw_backtranslation_en: This program can be wrong. It gives only a preliminary answer. The extension officer will make the final decision.
disclaimer_final_call.notes: Shown on every result screen and plot card. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): re-check of the revised line (Oct 3): meaning kept ('It gives only a preliminary answer'). Revised Oct 3 after the machine cross-check; see docs/SWAHILI_CHECK.md.

consent_photos.en: May I photograph some coffee leaves on your farm? The photos stay on this phone. We keep your co-op number in coded form, not your name. The officer may look at the photos. You can say no, or ask us to delete them later.
consent_photos.sw: Je, naweza kupiga picha za majani ya kahawa shambani mwako? Picha zitabaki kwenye simu hii. Hatuhifadhi jina lako. Tunahifadhi namba yako ya uanachama katika chama cha ushirika tu, na tunaiweka kuwa siri. Afisa wa ugani anaweza kuziangalia picha hizi. Unaweza kukataa, au kutuomba tuzifute baadaye.
consent_photos.sw_backtranslation_en: Can I take pictures of the coffee leaves in your field? The pictures will remain on this phone. We will not preserve your name. We only keep your membership number in the association, and we keep it confidential. An extension officer can look at these pictures. You may refuse, or you may ask us to delete it later.
consent_photos.notes: Read aloud by the relay farmer before the first photo. 'Coded form' = SHA-256 hash of the member number (pseudonymous, not anonymous). The Swahili says 'We do not keep your name. We keep only your membership number in the cooperative, and we keep it confidential' ('tunaiweka kuwa siri'); it has no separate word for 'coded'. Back-translation check (NLLB-600M, swh->eng, machine only): re-check of the revised line (Oct 3): meaning kept; 'namba yako ya uanachama' came back as 'membership number' and 'chama cha ushirika' as 'association'. Consent text should still be reviewed by a speaker before any real use. Revised Oct 3 after the machine cross-check; see docs/SWAHILI_CHECK.md.
